what: Port 8080 was already in use by another project's container, so Keycloak failed to take the default port.
why: Local environment conflict. The catalog does document keycloak_port as an override.
workaround: Set keycloak_port=8280 in judo.properties instead of the -o start option.
note: Port conflict was a local environment clash. build-process.md line 300 lists keycloak_port as a port override, and local-development.md covers start options.

what: Builder read the catalog through bash grep, sed and read for most of the first hour, instead of kb_search and kb_get. This is why the kb call share was low.
why: No kb-first rule was in the first prompt (the user later added it at line 723).
workaround: User steering at L723 and L756 changed the habit.
note: Orchestrator log R0 confirms 14 of ~460 calls were kb calls and no kb-first rule was in the first prompt; fixed by user steering. Process fix: put the kb-first rule in the build prompt template.

what: Builder ran validate, curl, log reads and browser checks between build steps. The user then said to check only at the end and to use kb for every question.
why: Check-as-you-go habit; the first prompt asked only for a final check.
workaround: Accepted the user rule at L906 and L907 for later rounds.
note: Log R0 confirms the check-as-you-go habit and the user rule to check only at the end. Run-specific prompt issue, nothing for the catalog.

what: A stale view-page identifier from before a restart gave INVALID_IDENTIFIER (400) in the browser, and the console showed Axios errors.
why: Signed identifiers become invalid after a restart. The catalog covers this in the Identifier Signing and signed identifier sections.
workaround: Cleared localStorage and sessionStorage and went back to the list.
note: Signed identifiers section and error-handling-guide.md (INVALID_IDENTIFIER) cover the stale-identifier error after restart. Builder hit it as an environment effect, not a gap.

what: Builder read that a custom visual element is a model-flagged extension point: set customImplementation on the element, then register an FC under CUSTOM_VISUAL_ELEMENT_INTERFACE_KEY with the per-element key from the container's customization.ts. The kb says there is no generic CUSTOM_COMPONENT_HOOK.
why: Only model-flagged elements can be replaced; the rest is covered by hooks and theming.
note: Claim is a restatement of what the kb says (customImplementation plus CUSTOM_VISUAL_ELEMENT_INTERFACE_KEY); the catalog paths exist. The real problems (table hook, view layout) are in other claims.

what: Builder used ask_user to ask permission for the application-customizer.tsx exception. The orchestrator corrected it: never use ask_user, write everything to the common channel.
why: Orchestrator rule for this run: questions go to the common channel, not ask_user.
workaround: Continued without further asking; decision recorded in GAPS.md.
note: Run rule: questions go to the common channel, not ask_user. Log R1 lists the customizer exception as accepted. Prompt-template item only.

what: Builder first concluded the generated project had no application/e2e module. The catalog switch exists: README 'Prerequisites > Enable E2E Generation' says set generateE2eModule=true. The first kb search did not surface that section.
why: E2E generation is off by default (generateE2eModule=false in generator-parameter.properties); the kb section was not the top hit for the first query.
workaround: Set generateE2eModule=true in generator-parameter.properties, ran build; application/e2e/webshop__shop was generated.
note: README lines 51-57 document generateE2eModule=true under Prerequisites. Retrieval problem: first kb search missed it; the builder found it after. The log R2 also says docs say only 'build' while generate and build are both needed (separate claim).

what: Session stopped just before the Round 2 report; the orchestrator resumed it and asked for the report again.
why: Session interruption, not a platform fault.
note: Log R2 notes the session was resumed once after a user stop. No platform or catalog content.

what: Builder checked the catalog for how users get created and found a managed-actor admin pattern and a multi-actor projection blueprint; no documented first-login user creation without custom code.
why: Catalog authentication guide says first-login insert must be done by an AuthenticationInterceptor until a release auto-inserts it (agent-docs/backend/authentication-guide.md).
note: Builder's finding is correct and the catalog already says auto-insert does not happen (authentication-guide.md line 84) and points to an AuthenticationInterceptor. Log R7 calls the interceptor 'platform (documented)'. Not a gap.

what: Builder read the generated LogAuthenticationInterceptor.java.default scaffold, the interceptors module, to plan the first-login user insert.
why: Catalog says managed actor auto-insert is not implemented in the runtime, so a custom AuthenticationInterceptor is needed.
note: Builder read the scaffold to plan the insert; catalog already documents the need for a custom AuthenticationInterceptor. Duplicate of c03-38.

what: Whole Playwright suite was not run as one command: the admin and customer modules ran separately, and the last customer test edit was not followed by an admin re-run.
why: After the module split the suite has two roots; the builder ran each one, not the whole.
workaround: Reported the split runs in the round report.
note: Log R13 records the same test-isolation lesson: new rule is per-round spec plus @smoke, full suites serial at the end. Builder habit after the module split.

what: The customer drawer profile showed the generated login name instead of the customer's name.
why: The default hero props use preferredUsername, which is a generated string for sign-ups and tests.
workaround: CustomHeroPropsHook in registerShellHooks.ts: given and family name from the token, then e-mail, then login name.
note: ui-hooks.md line 243 documents CustomHeroPropsHook. Possible small add: say the default uses preferredUsername, which is a generated login for sign-ups. Low value.

what: FUNCTIONS.md specifies the order status history as a post-call interceptor, which cannot fire for custom transition operations.
why: Interceptors run only for built-in operations; the spec was written without checking that rule, while the catalog states it correctly.
workaround: Each transition writes its history row inside the custom operation (OrderLifecycle.transition), in the same transaction.
note: interceptors.md says interceptors run for built-in CRUD only, never custom operations. The error was in FUNCTIONS.md (log R9: catalog correct). Fix FUNCTIONS.md, not the catalog.

what: FUNCTIONS.md specifies a range interceptor for the default 30-day order filter, but range interceptors fire only on reference range operations, not on list calls.
why: The spec assumed an interceptor could restrict a plain list; the catalog says a list needs an access definition or a list interceptor.
workaround: Modelled Admin.orders as a DERIVED access (orderedAt later than now minus 30 days) and added Admin.allOrders (ALL) so older orders stay reachable.
note: Catalog says range interceptors fire on reference ranges only; FUNCTIONS.md assumption was wrong (log R9). Derived access with now()!plusDays(-30) is covered by derived-access-filtering.

what: FUNCTIONS.md says delete deactivates a product that has orders; the catalog pattern refuses the delete with a fault and leaves deactivation to the user.
why: Spec and catalog pattern disagree on the behaviour.
workaround: Followed FUNCTIONS.md: removeProduct deactivates when orders exist; generic delete switched off (deleteable=false), removeProduct is the only delete.
note: Spec vs pattern mismatch in FUNCTIONS.md (log R9). The practice name already covers a deactivate fallback; builder followed the spec. Fix FUNCTIONS.md wording.

what: Interceptors fire only for built-in create, update, delete and reference operations; custom, mapped and script operations never reach them, so their guards and audit rows must sit inside the operation.
why: Stated by the builder from the kb and checked against interceptors.md; the catalog already says it.
note: Frontmatter of interceptors.md states built-in CRUD only, never custom, mapped or script operations. Duplicate of c05-06 root.

what: Range interceptors (getRangeFor and _getRangeReference) fire only on reference range lookups, not on plain list calls such as ~list.
why: Stated in interceptor-range-override.md; the builder relied on it to reject the FUNCTIONS.md design.
note: Same fact as c05-07, already in the catalog.

what: The Karaf runtime already contains PDFBox 2.0.13 and Handlebars 4.2.0 (karaf-offline assembly and karaf features), so no new bundle is needed for an invoice renderer.
why: Found by searching the built runtime; the catalog has no list of runtime-provided libraries.
note: Catalog says extra bundles (PDFBox, Handlebars) are added to the Karaf feature (best-practices osgi-karaf-bundle-architecture.md line 41), which is the opposite of the builder's finding that PDFBox 2.0.13 and Handlebars 4.2.0 already ship in the runtime. Not re-checked in the runtime assembly; mark verify. Add: 'Libraries already in the runtime (verify versions): PDFBox 2.0.13, Handlebars 4.2.0' and reconcile line 41.

what: Kb discipline: 10 kb_search and 5 kb_get calls against 208 bash and 45 read calls; the kb guard warned 52 times that source searching ran without a kb check; generated code and jars were read before the kb was consulted.
why: Builder defaulted to grep and generated-code reads; the round rule asks for kb first.
workaround: None; the guard warnings were ignored.
note: Log R11 records kb 15/269; the guard warned but did not block. Process finding: the guard is advisory only. Same root as c01-29.

what: Timestamp!now() in model expressions follows the platform defaultZoneId (UTC here), while LocalDateTime.now() in custom Java follows the JVM zone; the builder confirmed this against the DB (deliveredAt 05:29 vs UTC 04:29).
why: Two clocks in one platform; the catalog states it and the builder verified it against data.
note: 'Time and Time Zones' section says exactly this (lines 98-99). Log R12 says the earlier R11 claim of a platform bug was a builder mistake; the catalog was right.

what: Builder states that the generator adds every new column as a plain nullable column, so an existing row gets NULL and a required flag needs a backfill.
why: Builder read this from the kb (migration-backfill-default-where-null) and applied it.
note: Practice exists and the builder applied it (F52 first migration without wipe, log R12). The wipes in R6-R11 came from the schema-upgrade path problem, tracked in other claims.

what: Final full customer suite run was aborted by the tool (Command aborted), so the round's full-suite result is not in this chunk.
why: Cause not shown in the chunk.
note: Log R13 says the user stopped one over-long E2E run and the full suites at 3 workers failed from shared cart/stock; this abort is consistent with that. Cause not provable from the chunk.

what: kb use stayed low. The guard warned many times ('3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base'); the builder kept reading generated code, scratch scripts and jar internals before any kb lookup. Share was 7 of 298 calls in the previous round.
why: Builder habit: go to source first; the kb guard warns but does not stop it.
workaround: None in this chunk; user reminded the builder of the kb-first rule at each round start.
note: Log R13 records kb 7/298. Same root as c01-29: advisory guard, builder goes to source first.

what: Each rebuild cycle (generate, build, start, health check) took about 3 to 5 minutes with fixed sleeps of 200 to 280 seconds; the builder used full rebuilds for every UI change.
why: Full build loop used for frontend-only changes; no live dev server in this round.
note: Log R15 shows the orchestrator sent the live-iteration docs next round. development-workflow.md has an HMR section (line 96), so the content exists; the builder was not told to use it. Put 'use dev server and HMR for frontend-only changes' in the build prompt.
